title: HTI5007 Radiation Biology — Chapter 4 Protein Names: Decoder & Mnemonics
subtitle: Source: RadBio_Revision_Notes.pdf, Ch 4 pp. 93–125 and Ch 8 summary pp. 288–291

section1.heading: Decode the names (what biologists actually use)
rule_of_thumb: -ase = enzyme; kinase adds a phosphate, phosphatase removes one
Cdc / RAD / wee = yeast mutant names
ATM / NBS / Rb = named after a human disease

rows.name: p53, p21, p27, p16
rows.hook: Big number = big boss (p53). Small numbers (16, 21, 27) are the little wedges (CKIs) that jam a CDK

rows.name: CDK
rows.meaning: Cyclin-Dependent Kinase; numbers = order of discovery, not order in the cycle
rows.hook: That's why the cycle goes 4/6 → 2 → 2 → 1, not 1-2-3-4

rows.name: Cyclin
rows.meaning: Named because its level cycles up and down
rows.hook: Letters D, E, A, B = discovery order too

rows.name: Cdc25, Cdc2
rows.meaning: Cell Division Cycle mutant no. 25 / no. 2 (yeast)

rows.name: Wee1
rows.meaning: Yeast mutants lacking it divide too early → tiny "wee" cells
rows.hook: "Wee1 says Wait" (puts the tired-phosphate on Tyr)

rows.name: ATM / ATR
rows.hook: Named after the disease of patients who lack it

rows.name: CHK1, CHK2
rows.hook: Two broken strands (DSB) → ATM → CHK2; one strand (replication stress) → ATR → CHK1

rows.name: MRN = MRE11 + RAD50 + NBS1
rows.meaning: Meiotic REcombination 11, RADiation-sensitive 50, Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome 1
rows.hook: "Mr N" — the night-watchman who finds the break

rows.name: H2AX → γH2AX
rows.meaning: Histone H2A variant X; γ = the phosphorylated form
rows.hook: γ-rays leave γ-flags (foci) at each break

rows.name: MDM2
rows.meaning: Mouse Double Minute 2 (a gene amplified in mouse cells)

rows.name: CDKN1A (= p21)
rows.hook: The gene name of the bouncer

rows.name: Rb
rows.meaning: RetinoBlastoma (childhood eye tumour when it's lost)

rows.name: E2F
rows.hook: "Entry-to-S Factor" — the ignition key Rb holds

rows.name: Bax
rows.hook: "p53 swings the axe" at the mitochondrion

rows.name: Luciferase, GFP, Cas9, HSV1-tk, OTC
rows.meaning: light-bearer (Lucifer) enzyme; Green Fluorescent Protein; CRISPR-ASsociated 9; Herpes simplex virus 1 thymidine kinase; Ornithine TransCarbamylase

devices.title: Cyclin order through the cycle — "DEAB": Decide, Enter, Advance, Burst
items: Cyclin D – CDK4/6: G1, the cell Decides to divide
Cyclin E – CDK2: Enter S (G1/S border)
Cyclin A – CDK2: Advance through S and into G2 (the 2024 Q35 answer: CDK2 at S/G2)
Cyclin B – CDK1: Burst into mitosis (G2/M)
devices.extra: CDK partners: "4-6-2-2-1, like a countdown — the cycle counts down to 1 = mitosis (CDK1)." D takes the pair (4/6), E and A share 2, B gets 1.

devices.title: The five switches on a CDK — "B-CAK, Wee, Cdc, CKI"
items: Bind cyclin (on)
CAK on Thr (on)
Wee1 on Tyr (off)
Cdc25 strips Tyr-phosphate (on again)
CKI p21/p27/p16 (off)
devices.extra: Notes' own line (p. 101): Thr = thrive, Tyr = tired; add "Wee1 makes it Weary, Cdc25 is the Cure."

devices.title: The SQ1 chain (DSB → G1 arrest)
devices.story: Mr N calls ATM, ATM checks (CHK2) and flags (γH2AX); p53 escapes the MDM2 bodyguard, hires the p21 bouncer, who blocks cyclin E–CDK2; Rb keeps the key (E2F); no entry to S.

acronym.phrase: My ATM Card Pays Pocket Cash, Really Easy
acronym.expansion: MRN, ATM, CHK2, p53, p21, CDK2 blocked, Rb, E2F

devices.five_steps_label: Sense – Signal – Stabilise – Effector – Arrest (S-S-S-E-A), as in Problem 4.4

five_steps.name: Stabilise
five_steps.text: p53 escapes MDM2 and builds up

five_steps.name: Effector
five_steps.text: p53 switches on p21, p21 blocks cyclin E–CDK2 and cyclin D–CDK4/6

five_steps.name: Arrest
five_steps.text: Rb stays hypophosphorylated, holds E2F, cell stops at G1/S; outcome = repair / apoptosis / senescence

devices.title: The G2/M checkpoint (no p53) — "ATM/ATR → CHK1/2 ⊣ Cdc25 ⊣ CDK1"
items: "Checks Cancel the Cure" (CHK cancels Cdc25, so CDK1 stays weary)
Exam contrast: G1 arrest needs p53, G2 arrest does not — "G1 has 1 guardian; G2 goes without."
About half of human cancers have broken TP53.

devices.title: Checkpoint proteins (notes p. 96 table)
items: "G1 is a PERP" (p53, E2F, Rb, p21)
"Intra-S has 2 A's and 2 C's" (ATM, ATR, CHK1, CHK2)
"G2/M: CHK1 Cuts Cdc25, Cyclin B–CDK1"

devices.title: Apoptosis route — "p53 → Bax → cyt c → caspase-3"
items: "Bax Cracks the Cell" (Bax, Cytochrome c, Caspase)

devices.title: CKIs p16, p21, p27
items: "16-21-27: teenager, adult, late-twenties — all three refuse to let the CDK party start"
p21 is the one p53 orders (gene CDKN1A)

devices.title: Blots — standard SNoW DRoP
items: Southern–DNA, Northern–RNA, Western–Protein
Add: "Southern is the only person (Edwin Southern, 1975); the others are compass jokes."

devices.title: Gene delivery
items: "Trans-FORM-ation for bacteria (heat shock), trans-FECT-ion for eukaryote cells without virus (electroporation, sonoporation, calcium phosphate, Lipofectamine), trans-DUCT-ion needs a viral conDUCTor."
2024 Q2: heat-shock transformation cannot transfer genes into mammalian cells.

devices.title: Silencing (2024 Q29)
items: "si, sh, mi, CRISPR silence; mRNA is the Messenger — you don't silence a message by sending more of it."
siRNA transient; shRNA stable via vector; miRNA natural, blocks translation; CRISPR/Cas9 cuts the gene, permanent knockout.

devices.title: Vectors
items: Lentivirus = Long-term, Lazy cells (integrates, infects non-dividing, ~9 kb)
Adeno = Alarm (strong immune response, Jesse Gelsinger 1999)
AAV = Almost no Alarm but small
HSV = Huge capacity

section3.heading: How to make these stick
tips: Draw the SQ1 chain from memory every day (blank page, 2 minutes), then compare with Fig 4.2 / p. 102. The 11-step list collapses to the 5-step S-S-S-E-A answer that earns the marks.
Use the "tag" trick when reading: every time a name appears, say its expansion out loud ("checkpoint kinase 2"). After three readings the expansion is the memory, not the letters.
Group by role, not alphabet — sensors (MRN), transducers (ATM/ATR, CHK1/2), effectors (p53, p21, Cdc25), targets (cyclin–CDK, Rb, E2F). This matches how examiners phrase SQ1.
Put the DEAB and 4-6-2-2-1 lines on the same card as the Q35 fact (CDK2 at S/G2) — that's the one MC question drawn from this list.

standard_mnemonics_from_notes.meaning: phosphate on Thr activates a CDK, on Tyr inhibits it
